title: Regular base change for etale derived direct image
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. Let $h:Y\to X$ be a morphism between Noetherian schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible; Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Assume $h$ is regular: it is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and its fibres remain regular after every finite extension of the residue field [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Let $g:V\to X$ be any quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Form $V_Y=V\times_XY$ with projections $q:V_Y\to V$ and $g_Y:V_Y\to Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use bounded-below derived categories of constant $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and right derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every $K\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the canonical derived exchange morphism [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]
$$h^*Rg_*K\longrightarrow Rg_{Y,*}q^*K$$
is an isomorphism. For module coefficients the exchange is formed using the module adjunctions and transported constant coefficients, as in [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients]. No constructibility condition on $K$, finite-type condition on $h$, or Noetherian condition on $V$ is required.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 4.2.1, printed p. 281; specialized from locally Noetherian to Noetherian X and Y, with coefficient integer ell^n. The proposition is used directly, not its references to other sources.

from.place: Proof, Step 1: dimension-normalized Verdier duality in the lower perverse bound, via lem-per-qbar-arbitrary-field-duality and the regular generic duality model; the finite prime-power potential-dualizing pullback underlying that model. Supported exchange used to construct fibrewise costalk pinnings. Direct-image base change for the open complement is the input to the supported exchange argument.
